text:
ashley_arch: RFC follow-up 1: quick sync on an "escape-hatch" and compact policy translation layer for canary/A-B rollouts. core tension: local runtime needs to make sub-100ms fallback decisions while central observer provides stronger but slower signals. goal: clear interface + safe defaults.

ben_platform: agree. router/runtime should make the immediate decision (latency), and observer should publish consolidated signals (quality regressions, global error spikes). avoid leaking policy complexity to clients.

maria_dev: product asks for graded degradation before full rollback: reduce tokens, switch to quantized variant, then full fallback. need policy primitives to express that.

dave_oncall: ops requirement: if control-plane connectivity drops, runtimes must keep a deterministic runway (local counters + policy) so we don't flip-flop. soft-state is okay for short outages but must be deterministic on restart.

liam_infra: proposed runtime primitive: route-level "fallback_budget" (token bucket semantics). runtime consumes budget on each degraded decision; actions are ordered tiers. once budget exhausted, escalate to hard rollback. budget persists locally (redis AOF) and checkpoints to central store periodically.

ashley_arch: rough policy DSL sketch (compact, serializable):
```
policy {
  id: "roll-6298765432"
  conditions: [p95_latency > 200ms for 2m, eval_regression > 0.8% for 5m]
  actions: [hedge(percentage=10, variant=v2-small), degrade(max_tokens=128), fallback(variant=stable)]
  budget: {tokens: "1000", window: "1m"}
  default: "fallback-safe"
}
```
Key rules: unknown fields ignored, missing fields -> conservative safe defaults, and policy must be versioned.

maria_dev: we must standardize telemetry keys: rollout.id, variant.id, policy.version, budget.remaining, fallback.reason, signal.source. Without this, runbooks and automations break.

ben_platform: cross-region nuance: some variants may not exist in all regions. Observer offers a global verdict; router combines with local capability map and policy to pick the nearest compatible action. Route must prefer region-local compatible variants to avoid cross-region egress.

dave_oncall: avoid pagers for transient noise. recommend requiring N consecutive failing windows or using a decay-weighted score before triggering global paging. local fallbacks can be immediate but annotate the audit log.

maria_dev: tie auto-fallback thresholds to our eval-suite (reuse eval hooks). e.g., require alerting condition + eval-suite confirmation within X minutes for auto-rollback, or else only apply soft degradation.

deploy-bot: rollout 6298765432 started 1 model=gpt-x-lite variant=v2 canary=3% :rocket:

liam_infra: storage design: keep live budget counters and last-applied policy local (redis with AOF). persist snapshots every 30s to central KVS (etcd) for auditing and cold-start rehydrate. on restart, runtime replays local AOF, then reconciles with central snapshot and observer.

ben_platform: runtime->observer contract: tiny gRPC surface that returns a verdict object {verdict: pass|fail|degraded, reason_codes: [], ttl: 30s}. router merges verdict with local policy and capability map. always prefer safe fallback if unknown.

maria_dev: operational playbook: when an auto-fallback action runs, create an annotated entry (rollout.id, delta metrics, verdict) and only page on full rollback or customer-impacting errors. otherwise annotate the rollout audit trail and surface in console.

dave_oncall: add a manual escape-hatch on console: set route.fallback=off for a route/tenant with TTL and mandatory audit reason. also allow one-click rollback and a one-click resume.

ashley_arch: follow-ups (owners):
- maria_dev: proto for policy DSL and mapping of eval signals -> policy conditions
- ben_platform: draft gRPC decision API and telemetry tag contract
- liam_infra: redis AOF checkpointing and restore doc
- dave_oncall: oncall playbook + paging thresholds and smoothing heuristics
Plan: 30m sync tomorrow 10:00 to iterate on proto.

ben_platform: will post a minimal gRPC sketch in the doc and include example verdict codes.

maria_dev: will enumerate eval metrics and propose thresholds and consecutive-window logic.

deploy-bot: Canary progress (t+90s): p95 +12ms, eval_delta +0.2% 1 no actions triggered.

dave_oncall: I'll watch for escalation_count>2 and stand ready to intervene.

ashley_arch: wrapping up 1 keep the translation layer tiny, enforce conservative defaults, and ensure runtime autonomous behavior when disconnected. thanks everyone.
